clue.text: See a sign beside new farm, along with enclosure of good agricultural area

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, as in a cross-reference
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: enclosure of says the next piece is enclosed by the rearranged letters
new tells us the letters of the two words are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written into the pool of letters
taken as written into the pool of letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fertile stretch of land: a farm with a field enclosed by good fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' as V comes from vide, Latin for see. The Vale of Glamorgan is a county in south Wales known for its farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh county is a fertile lowland region long valued for farming, so it is an agricultural area.

clue.text: Looked up, having struggled to hold pose

indicators.note: to hold says the struggling word holds the pose inside it

parts.note: vied means competed or struggled
to sit is to pose for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone glanced up after wrestling to keep a difficult stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked up' means called in on someone, not raised one's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: To look someone up is an idiom for calling on them, the same as paying a visit.

clue.text: High-spirited man on bridge opponents charged

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a lad is a lively, spirited young man, a bit of a lad
in bridge the players are named by compass points, so East and North are opponents of the other pair

explanation.surface: A lively fellow at the bridge table accuses his opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means loaded, not accused.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged in the sense of loaded or filled, as a gun or a heavy cart is laden.

clue.text: Watchful Boers playing leading part over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the van piece above the next
playing suggests the letters of Boers are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army or procession

explanation.surface: Alert Afrikaner settlers take the lead in some game for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone alert who notices what is going on around them; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Walk from wicket for instance on declaration

indicators.note: on declaration says the word is to be spoken, so we go by its sound

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate, an example of one

explanation.surface: A cricketer walks off from the wicket after his side declares.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket 'declaration' ends an innings; here it means saying aloud. A wicket gate is a small door set in a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gait is a manner of walking, so the noun walk names the same thing.

clue.text: Put away leaflets used without frequency in workshops

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so put away means ate

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken out of the leaflets word

parts.note: fliers are printed leaflets handed out
F is the abbreviation for frequency in physics

explanation.surface: Flyers are stored and no longer handed out so often in the studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like tidying up but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a kind of workshop.

clue.text: No space for data concerning game

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing, so no
MB, a megabyte, is a measure of storage space for computer data
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A computer user grumbles that there is no room left for files about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: OMBRE is an old card game for three players.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a popular seventeenth-century card game, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Painting is article protected by screen

indicators.note: protected by says the inner pieces sit inside the screen word

parts.note: a grille is a grating that screens an opening
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A work of art is kept safe behind a protective screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisaille is a method of painting in shades of grey, and also a painting made that way.

clue.text: Item to write on drama followed by bit about recording

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: about says the bit word goes round the recording

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A writer's jotter follows a play, with a snippet on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of paper used for writing notes, so it is something to write on.

clue.text: Hands clean? That's critical, incidentally

parts.note: a hand can be a side, as in on every hand meaning on every side
to wipe is to clean

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether hands are washed, and remarks that it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' is not the body part: on the left hand means on the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing critical remark made while talking about something else is an incidental attack, a glancing blow.

clue.text: Objection to case one lawyer initially made

indicators.note: to case means to enclose, so the objection word holds the others

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of lawyer is used

explanation.surface: A lawyer starts off by raising an objection to a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a lawsuit but means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Built and made are synonyms, both past participles of putting something together.

clue.text: Colour with skill around mystical writing

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the skill word is read backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Someone adds colour skilfully to a mystical manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantras are Hindu and Buddhist religious texts of mystical and ritual teaching.

clue.text: Excited by device increasing volume? It's a gas

parts.note: fired, as in fired up, means excited
an amp, an amplifier, makes sound louder

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a loud amplifier calls it great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a gas' sounds like slang for great fun, but literally names a gas. FIREDAMP is the explosive methane found in coal mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane collecting in coal mines, which is a gas in the literal sense.

clue.text: Junk child put back in order

indicators.note: put back says the two pieces together are written in reverse

parts.note: tat is cheap junk or rubbish
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to put the rubbish back where it belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consent, an order from above.

clue.text: Weed got roughed up in ranks, adapted and then succeeded

indicators.note: in places that rearrangement inside the other
adapted says the letters of ranks are changed into another arrangement
roughed up suggests the letters of got are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A weed got trampled in the rows, but adapted and then flourished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughed up' and 'adapted' each signal an anagram; 'in' sets the first inside the second. Knotgrass is a common weed of waste ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotgrass is a low-growing plant common on waste ground and in gardens, where it counts as a weed.

clue.text: Ran glowing feature on magical act

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the glowing feature after the magical act

parts.note: a trick is a conjuring act
an LED, a light-emitting diode, is a small glowing component

explanation.surface: A light display flickers on during a conjurer's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: An LED is a light-emitting diode, a small glowing component.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickled means flowed slowly, as liquid runs in a thin stream.

clue.text: Rook, young one in the field

parts.note: to rook is to swindle, as is to con
tender means young, as in at a tender age

explanation.surface: A rook, a young bird, stands in a farmer's field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the bird, or a chess piece, but means cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The field is all the competitors in a race, so a contender is one of them.

clue.text: I delay going up to meet Swede, man of influence

parts.note: Sven is a typical Swedish man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the pieces are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lag means delay

explanation.surface: Someone stalls before climbing to meet an influential Swedish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to meet' joins the pieces. Svengali, the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, gives his name to anyone who controls another.
explanation.definitionFit: A svengali is a person who exerts a controlling, often sinister, influence over someone else.

clue.text: Left overwhelmed by strain, lacking heart to be merry

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the left word is swallowed up inside another
lacking heart says the central letter is removed from the strain word

parts.note: to strain liquid is to sieve it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Feeling crushed by the pressure, a person has lost the will to enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress but means filter; 'lacking heart' drops its middle letter, leaving SIVE, and 'overwhelmed by' puts the left word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful or frolicsome, close in sense to merry.

clue.text: Woman raised need for varnish

parts.note: she refers to a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: call means need, as in there is no call for it

explanation.surface: A woman points out that a coat of varnish is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in alcohol and used as a varnish or polish.

clue.text: Joint enterprise would be hollow without this aim

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the phrase, so taking it out would leave the phrase empty in the middle

explanation.surface: A partnership has no point unless it shares a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters running from the second letter of 'Joint' into 'enterprise' and only the shells of those words are left.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is a purpose or intention, the thing one is aiming at.

clue.text: Effort to defend old story ending unhappily

indicators.note: to defend says the effort word surrounds and guards the other piece

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort
aged means old

explanation.surface: A struggle to protect an elderly person ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a drama or tale in which the main character comes to a disastrous end.

clue.text: Taking part and winning

definitions.meaning: winning in the sense of charming, attractive

explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means participating, as in engaging in debate, and also charming, as in an engaging smile.

clue.text: Saw statue standing on border?

definitions.meaning: a saw is an old saying or maxim
a garden ornament figure stood on a flower border

explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a pithy maxim, and also a small figure of a bearded dwarf placed in gardens.

clue.text: Hat supplied with distinctive quality? So it's said

parts.note: fed means supplied, as in fed with information

indicators.note: says the preceding word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality surrounding someone

explanation.surface: A hat comes with a special air, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech AURA and ORA sound alike, the R not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a brim and a creased crown.

clue.text: Jump aside from black cat

indicators.note: aside from says one letter is put aside from the jump word

parts.note: to bounce is to jump
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A black cat leaps out to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a large wild cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Pass on latest pieces of news, voracious for this?

definitions.text: Pass on latest pieces of news, voracious for this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: to go is to pass, as when a player passes their turn

indicators.note: latest pieces of picks the last letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: People hungry for the latest news pass it on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: tittle-tattle passed on by those greedy for it. GOSS is British slang for gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for gossip, the latest news passed around by people eager for it.

clue.text: Plain deal's ending with arrangement of loan

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of deal's
arrangement of says the letters of loan are put in another order

explanation.surface: A straightforward deal concludes with a loan agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective, simple, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain in South America, so the word names a plain.

clue.text: Bird mostly seen around island, twitching and ducking

indicators.note: around says the shortened bird goes round the following pieces
mostly says the bird word loses its last letter

parts.note: the avocet is a wading bird

indicators.note: twitching suggests the letters of and jerk about into a new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a wader near an island while out twitching, and ducks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' is birdwatching slang, but here an anagram signal giving DAN; 'mostly' drops the bird's last letter, leaving AVOCE, which goes around I and DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducking a duty means evading it, and avoidance is the act of doing so.

clue.text: Work that's altered looks swell? Because satisfied, I shout about that

parts.note: cos is a casual short form of because
met, as in met a need, means satisfied

indicators.note: about says the shout word goes round the swell word

parts.note: to cry is to shout
a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in delight because their facelift looks great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like slang for great but is the noun, a surge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery is an operation done purely to change someone's appearance, so it is work altering looks.
